title: Scientific Identity Verification — Certification
reframing_note: This phase was originally scoped as "fix the cheese scientific_name issue" based on findings in reports/content-quality-audit/entity-sampling.md and eeat-analysis.md (carried from AQ-01/AQ-01R/AQ-01R2) and reports/publication-integrity-certification.json (AQ-02B4). Reading docs/CHEESE_GOVERNANCE.md §5 before making any change revealed that finding was itself incorrect: scientific_name for cheese is explicitly, intentionally, and consistently governed to mean milk-source species, not cheese identity. All 204 cheese entities were verified to conform exactly to the documented 4-entry mapping table (cow/goat/sheep/buffalo), 0 mismatches. That finding is retracted — see reports/aq-03-retraction-notice.md. This phase instead ran a genuine, governance-aware, full-census verification across all 11 domains.
methodology: For each domain, scientific_name semantics were read directly from that domain's governance document (not assumed) before checking conformance. Ten domains define it as the entity's own primary species/botanical identity (or an explicit Multiple species/Multiple sources escape value for blends); cheese is the sole documented exception (milk-source species). Format validation accounts for standard botanical conventions (hybrid notation ×, spp. for multi-species genera, subgenus references) rather than a naive Genus-species regex, after an initial version of this check produced 6 false positives by not accounting for these conventions (loganberry, marionberry, plantain, strawberry, triticale, savory — all verified correct on inspection).

finding_detail.issue: scientific_name is "Rubus L. subgenus" — incomplete compared to all 5 sibling Rubus-family entries in the same catalog, which correctly show full binomials or hybrid notation (blackberry: Rubus fruticosus; raspberry: Rubus idaeus; boysenberry: Rubus ursinus × idaeus; loganberry: Rubus × loganobaccus; tayberry: Rubus fruticosus × idaeus).
finding_detail.action_taken: NOT corrected in this pass. Marionberry is a multi-generation cultivar ('Chehalem' × 'Olallie' blackberry, itself complex Rubus ursinus-lineage parentage) without one universally-agreed single binomial — real botanical nomenclature nuance exists for cultivar parentage notation that this audit is not positioned to resolve by assumption (Rule 3: never replace one assumption with another). Recommended for a future editorial pass with proper botanical sourcing, using the sibling entries' hybrid-notation convention as the pattern to follow once the correct parentage citation is confirmed.

overall_result: PASS (1 non-blocking data-completeness finding, deferred to editorial review)
